body:
## Goal

Report a named claim denial when opening a transition-lock file fails, so serve_once can continue serving without weakening transition exclusion.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Force OSError at the transition-lock open boundary and assert a named claim denial instead of a propagated exception.
- [ ] Drive serve_once again after the denied claim and verify that it continues serving.
- [ ] Take no resource tokens on denial; preserve busy-lock, successful-lock, and claim-body exception behavior.

## Likely files

- `src/prismabuild/_measurement_reservation.py`
- `tests/test_measurement_reservation_census_1419.py`
- `tests/test_transition_lock_denial_1515.py`

## Context

Source issue: https://github.com/RobTand/prismabuild/issues/1515

https://github.com/RobTand/prismabuild/pull/1514#issuecomment-5985595510

Related: https://github.com/RobTand/prismabuild/issues/1514

<details><summary>Original text</summary>

Question raised by the independent review of PR #1514 (APPROVE at `47336e49`, https://github.com/RobTand/prismabuild/pull/1514#issuecomment-5985595510). Filed by the issues lead, record `issues-burndown`.

Inside `locked_census` (`src/prismabuild/_measurement_reservation.py`), a raw `OSError` from opening a transition-lock file propagates to `serve_once` instead of becoming a claim denial. That is the behaviour before PR #1502, which PR #1502 had accidentally changed and PR #1514 restores. Every other lock outcome is a named refusal: `AdmissionBusy` gives `claim()` returning None, `AdmissionUnavailable` gives a `host_admission_unavailable` denial, and a busy transition key gives `CensusUnavailable`.

**Question:** should an unopenable transition-lock file also be a named claim denial, so one bad lock file cannot surface as an exception in the worker loop? Not measured: whether `serve_once` already contains this `OSError` safely, and whether it has ever occurred on the fleet.

**Severity: P3.** It is a pre-existing behaviour, restored rather than introduced, and no decision rides on it today. Raise it if a worker loop is ever seen to stop on it.

Filer chose to file rather than fix: it is a behaviour choice about the admission gate, and PR #1514 was approved as a minimal restoration.

</details>
title: [P3] Turn unopenable transition locks into claim denials
